summary: The minister set out [242 services live, over 270 by end-2026 and about 450 by 2030](2026-07-21-ahram-ict-minister-450-digital-services-2030).
developments:
The base's last count before the window is [more than 170 e-government services](2024-09-30 5 facts about Digital Public Infrastructure (UNDP Egypt)), with no target series on record.

2026-07-21 - the minister [set out 242 services, a target of over 270 by end-2026 and about 450 by 2030, under a legislation and governance pillar alongside digital transformation, technology localisation, digital infrastructure and capacity building](2026-07-21-ahram-ict-minister-450-digital-services-2030), the [nearer target having been stated in June](2026-06-20-egypt-50-new-services-270-target-2026-ahram).

The targets are ministerial statements to investor and press audiences rather than a published plan, and no delivery report against the 2026 figure has appeared.

summary: [105 government entities are connected and 242 services live on the national platform](2026-07-19-rabt-105-jiha-hukumiyya-242-khidma-mansat-misr-al-raqmiyya), under the [ICT 2030 strategy](2026-01-01-misr-al-raqmiyya-istratijiyyat-al-ittisalat-wa-tiknulujia-al-maalumat-2030).
developments:
The strategy runs on [three pillars of digital transformation, digital skills and jobs, and technological innovation](2026-01-01-misr-al-raqmiyya-istratijiyyat-al-ittisalat-wa-tiknulujia-al-maalumat-2030).

2026-01-02 - the ministry's annual statement puts [the national platform at 210 services and 10.7 million users, and a 47-place improvement in an international ranking](2026-01-02-mcit-egypt-ict-sector-achievements-2025).

2026-07-19 - a cabinet follow-up meeting recorded [105 government entities connected electronically and 242 services available on the platform](2026-07-19-rabt-105-jiha-hukumiyya-242-khidma-mansat-misr-al-raqmiyya) - 32 more services in six months, on the government's own count.

summary: A [2026-2030 spectrum strategy accompanied a US$3.5bn award of 410 MHz to the four operators](2026-02-10-egypt-3-5b-spectrum-deal-5g-connectingafrica), doubling their holdings.
developments:
Neither existed at the window's opening. [410 MHz of additional spectrum was awarded across 1.8 GHz, 2.6 GHz and 3.5 GHz, doubling operator holdings in a single transaction, for US$3.5bn paid to the regulator, the minister stating the award matches all spectrum allocated in the country over the previous thirty years](2026-02-10-egypt-3-5b-spectrum-deal-5g-connectingafrica).

The strategy document is not held. The country [refarmed 2.6 GHz for fifth-generation service rather than licensing dedicated mid-band, and set no coverage or speed obligations comparable to its neighbours'](2026-08-03-ookla-5g-north-africa-one-year-on) - so the largest spectrum transaction on this ledger carries no published obligation on what the operators must deliver with it. Investment [since 2019 is stated at more than US$6bn, with about 3,000 new towers planned in-year and a stated target of 40,000 by 2028](2026-06-02-egypt-6bn-telecom-investment-since-2019-techafricanews), in dollars by the ministry and with no split between state and operator spending given.

summary: A [national data-centre strategy is under preparation on presidential directive](2026-06-30-egypt-national-data-centre-strategy-sovereignty-ahram), framed around localisation and a regional hub.
developments:
The strategy did not exist at the window's opening. It is [under preparation, framed around data localisation, a regional storage and processing hub, digital sovereignty and digital-services exports](2026-06-30-egypt-national-data-centre-strategy-sovereignty-ahram), [reaffirmed by Cabinet on 5 July 2026](2026-07-05-egypt-cabinet-giant-data-centres-ai-youm7) and [by the minister on 21 July](2026-07-21-ahram-ict-minister-450-digital-services-2030). No publication date, draft text or governing instrument is held, and the ministry says data-centre licensing continues to expand in the meantime.

So the licensing regime is running ahead of the policy that would frame it: ten licences issued in two years, and a strategy still being written.

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: The ministry names [linking government digital systems as the strategic objective](2026-01-01-mcit-digital-government-digital-transformation); no framework or roadmap is published.
developments:
The ministry's programme page for digital government [names data as a main transformation platform and the linking of government digital systems as the strategic objective](2026-01-01-mcit-digital-government-digital-transformation). No published national interoperability framework accompanies it.

What exists instead is a count of connections: [105 government entities connected electronically and 242 services on the national platform as at July 2026](2026-07-19-rabt-105-jiha-hukumiyya-242-khidma-mansat-misr-al-raqmiyya).

A connection count is not a framework. Nothing states the standard those 105 entities connected against, or what a 106th would have to meet.

summary: The [second-edition strategy for 2025-2030 stands unchanged](2026-06-10-egypt-ai-national-security-strategy-karnak-ahram), with delivery bodies added around it.
developments:
The second edition has been [in force from early 2025 on six pillars covering governance, technology, data, infrastructure, the sector and skills, following a first strategy of 2021 and a responsible-artificial-intelligence charter of 2023](2026-06-10-egypt-ai-national-security-strategy-karnak-ahram), and is [restated by the minister without revision](2026-07-21-ahram-ict-minister-450-digital-services-2030). The text is not held, and the country is [counted among those regulating artificial intelligence by strategy rather than statute](2026-07-28-how-african-governments-are-regulating-ai).

What was added around it: the [council created in 2019 had its remit widened to artificial intelligence, quantum computing and emerging technologies and is preparing a national quantum strategy, with no decree, membership list or rename date held](2026-06-10-egypt-ai-national-security-strategy-karnak-ahram), and a [university capacity programme is placed under the strategy](2026-08-04-egypt-mcit-ai-capacity-building-universities).

summary: A [national open data policy is named in passing by the minister](2025-12-21-egypt-world-bank-gtmi-22nd-group-a-ahram) with no date, text, portal or dataset inventory established.
developments:
The base carries no statement of the policy's existence or content at the window's opening. The minister [named the launch of the open data policy among the policies and legislation supporting digital transformation](2025-12-21-egypt-world-bank-gtmi-22nd-group-a-ahram), and no date of adoption, text, issuing instrument, dataset inventory or national portal is established.

A single passing ministerial reference is the entire evidence base for this instrument. It sits alongside a governance framework that ranks the country twenty-second in the world on govtech maturity, which is the gap this indicator records: high measured maturity, and no published data.

summary: The [2020 data-protection law was operationalised by Executive Regulations issued on 1 November 2025](2026-02-11 Egypt finalises Executive Regulations to the PDPL (Decree 816-2025)), enforceable from 1 November 2026.
developments:
The law had been [in force since 2020 and never operationalised, with no executive regulations issued](2026-02-11 Egypt finalises Executive Regulations to the PDPL (Decree 816-2025)) - which is why the [Alexandria Economic Court decided a mobile-operator case in February 2025 on tort grounds](2025-09-02 Egyptian court judgment tightens data-protection enforcement (Orange Egypt)), more than four years after the law passed.

The Regulations were [issued by ministerial decree on 1 November 2025 and circulated in December, establishing the approvals model, a separate licence for each cross-border transfer specifying destination, purpose, data categories and safeguards, extra approvals for electronic marketing and certain public-space surveillance, registered data-protection officers, and breach notification within seventy-two hours to the regulator and three business days to affected individuals](2026-02-11 Egypt finalises Executive Regulations to the PDPL (Decree 816-2025)). The obligations become enforceable from 1 November 2026 at the end of a one-year grace period. The Regulations' own text is not held.

summary: A [regulatory framework for cybersecurity services](2024-06-01-ntra-al-itar-al-tanzimi-li-khadamat-al-amn-al-sibrani) rests on the 2018 crimes law, which [two bills would now amend](2026-04-22-tadilat-qanun-175-2018-jaraim-al-dhaka-al-istinai).
developments:
The regulator's [operative framework for providing cybersecurity services rests on the 2018 information technology crimes law and the 2003 telecommunications regulation law](2024-06-01-ntra-al-itar-al-tanzimi-li-khadamat-al-amn-al-sibrani).

2026-04-22 - two separately sponsored private members' bills would amend the 2018 law: one [to strengthen protection of children against newly emerging electronic crimes](2026-04-22-mashru-qanun-hamayat-al-atfal-min-al-jaraim-al-iliktruniyya), the other [to address artificial-intelligence-generated deepfakes and tie fines to the benefit obtained](2026-04-22-tadilat-qanun-175-2018-jaraim-al-dhaka-al-istinai). Neither is recorded as passed.

The regulator also [signed a cross-border cyber security cooperation agreement with a Gulf council in October 2025](2025-10-19-ntra-uae-cybersecurity-council-framework-agreement-gitex).

summary: A [member's proposal for a biometric national identity card for children from age five was discussed at two workshops](2026-04-19-egypt-child-national-id-biometric-registry-proposal-youm7); no bill is tabled.
developments:
Nothing of the kind was on record at the window's opening. A [member's proposal for a national identity card for children carrying a photograph from age five, requiring amendment of the Child Law, was discussed at two workshops, with recommendations including a unified national child-data platform, a full biometric identification system for children, and linkage between health, education and other government databases](2026-04-19-egypt-child-national-id-biometric-registry-proposal-youm7). Participants also recommended a strict legal framework for protecting the resulting data.

No bill has been tabled. The country's identity layer - a digital identity app, a financial identity system, a biometric authentication pilot and facial verification at mobile-line enrolment - all now operates with no statute of its own, and the only identity legislation on the record is a proposal to extend it to children.

summary: The central bank approved [regulations for a digital financial identity platform](2026-08-23-cbe-digital-financial-identity-platform-ekyc-regulations) and the financial regulator [admitted two projects to its sandbox](2026-09-01-techafricanews-egypt-fra-fintech-sandbox).
developments:
2025-09 - the central bank issued [regulations on governance, internal control and fit-and-proper criteria for key officials of payment system operators and payment service providers](2025-09-01-cbe-governance-internal-control-fit-and-proper-payment-institutions) - the conduct rules beneath the payments market.

2026-08-23 - its board [approved the regulations governing the digital financial identity platform for identifying bank customers and verifying their identities electronically](2026-08-23-cbe-digital-financial-identity-platform-ekyc-regulations), which is the rule that lets an account be opened without a counter.

2026-09-01 - the financial regulator [granted preliminary approval for two further technology projects to enter its regulatory sandbox](2026-09-01-techafricanews-egypt-fra-fintech-sandbox).

No licence issued under the payment-institution rules, and no count of customers identified through the platform, appears on this ledger.

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: The [data centre and cloud licensing framework](2021-08-19-ntra-al-itar-al-tanzimi-li-insha-wa-tashghil-marakiz-al-bayanat) is the operative rule; no interoperability statute is held.
developments:
The regulator's [licensing and registration framework for establishing and operating data centres and providing hosting and cloud computing services](2021-08-19-ntra-al-itar-al-tanzimi-li-insha-wa-tashghil-marakiz-al-bayanat) is the operative rule beneath the estate, issued under the telecommunications law.

The one law that obliges an exchange is sectoral: [the 2025 real estate identifier law establishes a unified non-repeating national identifier database built on a unified base map](2025-06-17-egypt-law-88-2025-unified-real-estate-id-database), which is a shared key by statute.

No general statute requiring public bodies to exchange data, and no once-only rule, appears anywhere on this ledger.

summary: The minister told Cabinet a [regulator unit already detects and acts on artificial-intelligence-manipulated content](2026-07-29-youm7-national-body-unit-social-media-violations), and legislative amendment is needed.
developments:
2026-07-29 - the minister [told Cabinet that a unit had been formed inside the telecommunications regulator which already detects and acts on manipulated video and imagery, but that legislative amendment is needed to address the practices at root](2026-07-29-youm7-national-body-unit-social-media-violations). The unit's formation date, legal basis, staffing, method, appeal route and contest procedure are not stated: the detection capability operates ahead of the instrument that would authorise it.

At the same meeting the [Cabinet agreed a review of the governing social-media statutes, heavier financial penalties and public awareness campaigns, with a comparative study of other states' approaches being prepared and no bill, text or timetable stated](2026-07-29-youm7-national-body-unit-social-media-violations); the Prime Minister credited a press and media campaign with prompting the response.

summary: A [54-article party draft on the digital space would oblige platforms to appoint a legal representative and register influencers](2026-08-10-egypt-digital-space-law-mp-bahi); it is not tabled.
developments:
Nothing of the kind was on record at the window's opening. The draft was [described by its sponsor on 10 August 2026 as fifty-four articles across seven chapters, requiring digital platforms to appoint a legal representative in the country and register influencers on a national platform, and regulating artificial intelligence, deepfakes, online extortion, gambling and child protection online](2026-08-10-egypt-digital-space-law-mp-bahi).

It is not tabled and no text is published; the article count and the preparation time are the sponsoring member's own account, and it is separate from the cabinet's own social-media legislative review. So the most comprehensive platform instrument on this ledger exists only as a member's description of it.

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: The governing statute is [the 1960 statistics and census law](1960-02-09-qanun-35-lisanat-1960-fi-shan-al-ihsa-wal-tadad); no replacement is on the record.
developments:
The statistics agency publishes [the 1960 statute under its own heading of the laws regulating statistical work; its article 1 vests censuses and statistics in a technical body constituted by presidential decree](1960-02-09-qanun-35-lisanat-1960-fi-shan-al-ihsa-wal-tadad). It is sixty-six years old and the base holds no amendment or replacement.

2026-02-02 - the machinery under it moved: [the prime minister chaired the high committee for the 2027 population, housing and establishments census, with the agency and six ministers](2026-02-02-prime-minister-chairs-high-committee-2027-census).

A national statistics strategy [had been in preparation for nearly two years with 18 ministries and research bodies plus international partners](2024-06-10-minister-of-planning-discusses-national-statistics-strategy) and is not published.

summary: Two [freedom of information bills were submitted to parliament](2026-08-10-journalists-syndicate-submits-foi-bill-to-parliament) in August 2026; nothing is enacted.
developments:
2026-07-05 - the minister of state for information [told the prime minister that coordination was under way with ministries and authorities to issue the freedom of information law quickly](2026-07-05-egypt-coordinates-to-issue-freedom-of-information-law).

2026-08-09 - a member's bill was [submitted to the House with its text carried in the reporting](2026-08-09-awwal-mashru-qanun-li-hurriyyat-tadawul-al-maalumat).

2026-08-10 - a [syndicate-backed bill was submitted after securing 60 lawmakers' signatures; it would create an authority for the protection of freedom of information](2026-08-10-journalists-syndicate-submits-foi-bill-to-parliament).

Two bills and a ministerial statement of intent, with no statute in force, is the position after a decade of the same commitment.

summary: The [supervisory centre was confirmed by the Executive Regulations](2026-02-11 Egypt finalises Executive Regulations to the PDPL (Decree 816-2025)) and [published ten compliance guidelines](2026-06-23 Bimonthly Update on Privacy in Africa (January & February 2026)); no regulator decision is held.
developments:
The base carries no dated statement of the Centre's standing, staffing or activity at the window's opening. It is [confirmed as the body implementing, monitoring and enforcing the law, running the approvals and cross-border-transfer licensing regime, officer registration and breach receipt](2026-02-11 Egypt finalises Executive Regulations to the PDPL (Decree 816-2025)), its acting chief executive having [framed data sovereignty as a strategic necessity at a November 2025 workshop](2025-11-16-egypt-data-sovereignty-pdpc-cairo-ict-ahram).

2026-01 to 02 - [ten guidelines were published covering consent, lawful bases, electronic direct marketing, the data protection officer, officer categories, data users, principles, records of processing, licences and permits, and privacy notices, with breach-notification and records templates](2026-06-23 Bimonthly Update on Privacy in Africa (January & February 2026)).

Enforcement is one court award: [EGP 10 million ordered against an operator in February 2025 on tort and custodian's liability, not on the data-protection law](2025-09-02 Egyptian court judgment tightens data-protection enforcement (Orange Egypt)). No regulator decision, fine, registration figure or transfer licence is on record at any date.

summary: Rights organisations [called for withdrawal of the directives making biometric verification a condition of holding a mobile line](2026-08-24-eipr-egypt-biometric-telecom-registration).
developments:
2026-08-24 - organisations [called on the regulator to withdraw the directives making biometric verification a condition of registering, managing or recovering a mobile line, arguing that the regulator has published neither an account of where registration failed nor any assessment of whether the operators it referred to prosecution on 10 August can protect biometric data](2026-08-24-eipr-egypt-biometric-telecom-registration); the [objection was also put by a senator](2026-08-16-parlgate-senator-face-biometric-sim-objection). No regulatory instrument, retention rule or operator-side safeguard is held.

Parliament is meanwhile arguing for instruments that already exist: a member [demanded a comprehensive digital-privacy bill without referencing the 2020 law at any point](2026-07-20-ahram-mp-digital-privacy-legislation-demand), and another [proposed a national register letting citizens see which bodies have processed their data, arguing the 2020 law needs enforcement rather than replacement](2026-08-24-ahram-egypt-mp-national-register-personal-data-use).

summary: The country [chairs the Arab artificial-intelligence governance and quantum computing working groups](2026-07-31-egypt-arab-ai-governance-quantum-chairmanship), elected to two of six.
developments:
Neither chairmanship existed at the window's opening; the Arab permanent committee for artificial intelligence and emerging technologies was created by ministerial resolution at a session this country hosted in January 2026 and held its first founding meeting in May.

2026-07-31 - it was [elected chair of the artificial-intelligence governance working group, whose remit is a guidance framework, technical tools and mechanisms for activating the Arab charter for artificial-intelligence ethics, and of the quantum computing working group, whose remit is an Arab quantum strategy and quantum-cybersecurity deployment](2026-07-31-egypt-arab-ai-governance-quantum-chairmanship).

The committee is mandated to propose regional agreements and coordinate a unified position - a bloc track running alongside rather than through the continental work.

On the continental side the central bank hosts a [digital portal for the African financial stability committee, carrying its objectives, mandate and structure, its member central banks, its meeting calendar and working groups, and acting as the publication channel for the African Financial Stability Report and technical papers, its content maintained by the committee secretariat](2026-08-03-cbe-aacb-afsc-digital-portal).

summary: The [29th session of the Arab ICT ministers council approved an AI committee and adopted an ethics charter](2026-01-22-arab-ict-ministers-council-29th-session-cairo) in Cairo.
developments:
2026-01-22 - the 29th session, hosted by the communications ministry in Cairo, [approved the establishment of a regional committee for artificial intelligence and emerging technologies and adopted a regional charter on artificial-intelligence ethics, described as a guiding and advisory document rather than a binding instrument](2026-01-22-arab-ict-ministers-council-29th-session-cairo).

A guiding charter is harmonisation by persuasion. Nothing records the charter being domesticated here or anywhere, and the country's own [national governance framework](2026-03-15-guide-to-egypt-national-ai-governance-framework) is separately made and does not cite it.

summary: [2Africa lands at two Egyptian coasts joined by trans-Egypt routes](2025-11-19-telecom-egypt-completion-of-2africa), and a [point of presence opened at a Jordanian hub](2025-09-22-telecom-egypt-pop-aqaba-digital-hub).
developments:
The transit position is stated in figures: [click-to-order cross-connectivity between the 14 subsea systems landing at ten cable stations, linked over ten terrestrial routes](2023-09-27-telecom-egypt-launch-weconnect).

2025-11-19 - [2Africa lands at Ras Ghareb on the Red Sea and Port Said on the Mediterranean, the two joined by two trans-Egypt routes adjacent to the canal](2025-11-19-telecom-egypt-completion-of-2africa).

2025-09-22 - a [new point of presence at a Jordanian digital hub, paired with a subsea cable and a 15-kilometre link from a Sinai landing point](2025-09-22-telecom-egypt-pop-aqaba-digital-hub) opened a second-country interconnection, and [a binding offer valued the regional data hub at US$230m rising to US$260m](2025-09-07-telecom-egypt-helios-binding-offer-regional-data-hub).

summary: Executive regulations [set the conditions, procedures and fees for a cross-border transfer licence](2025-11-01-egypt-decision-816-2025-pdpl-executive-regulations), five years after the law provided for them.
developments:
Cross-border transfer is governed by [the 2020 personal data protection law, issued at the presidency on 13 July 2020 with entry into force three months later](2020-07-13-egypt-law-151-2020-personal-data-protection).

2025-11 - the executive regulations [set the conditions and procedures for a licence or permit to transfer personal data across borders, for legal and for natural persons, and the fees for it](2025-11-01-egypt-decision-816-2025-pdpl-executive-regulations).

Five years passed between the law and the regulations that make its transfer regime operable, and no licence, permit or refusal issued under them appears on this ledger.

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: The one sectoral exchange standard held is [the smart-metering adoption of 2025](2025-10-01-eos-7982-1-2025-electricity-metering-data-exchange-dlms-cosem); no whole-of-government standard is on the base.
developments:
The base holds one exchange standard and it is sectoral: [a 2025 national standard adopting the international smart-metering data-exchange standard](2025-10-01-eos-7982-1-2025-electricity-metering-data-exchange-dlms-cosem). Another is a specification rather than a standard: [a national electronic receipt technical specification setting the document element, data structure and mandatory fields for education-service return receipts exchanged with the tax authority](2026-08-03-eta-education-return-receipt-v1-2-data-structure).

No whole-of-government interoperability framework, message standard or conformity test appears anywhere, and the ministry's own programme page names [linking government digital systems as the strategic objective](2026-01-01-mcit-digital-government-digital-transformation) without one.

summary: A [2025 national standard adopts the international smart-metering data-exchange standard](2025-10-01-eos-7982-1-2025-electricity-metering-data-exchange-dlms-cosem), on a [default to international standards](2022-01-01-eos-al-muwasafat-al-tarif-bil-muwasafat-al-duwaliyya-wal-ajnabiyya).
developments:
The body is [the sole official one for preparing and issuing national standards, founded by presidential decree in 1957](2024-01-01-nashat-al-hayaa-al-misriyya-al-amma-lil-muwasafat-wal-jawda).

A ministerial decision of 2022 provides that [where no national standard exists, an international or foreign standard applies, from a named list](2022-01-01-eos-al-muwasafat-al-tarif-bil-muwasafat-al-duwaliyya-wal-ajnabiyya) - a default that makes the national catalogue a supplement rather than a gate.

2025-10 - the register carries [a national standard adopting the international smart-metering data-exchange standard](2025-10-01-eos-7982-1-2025-electricity-metering-data-exchange-dlms-cosem), giving electricity metering a common exchange basis.

summary: The central bank [formed an inter-ministerial working group on a sustainable finance taxonomy on 7 August 2026](2026-08-07-egypt-cbe-sustainable-finance-taxonomy-working-group).
developments:
Nothing of the kind was held at the window's opening. 2026-08-07 - a taxonomy is [under development by an inter-ministerial working group formed by the central bank with the finance, investment, environment and financial-regulatory authorities, ahead of official issuance](2026-08-07-egypt-cbe-sustainable-finance-taxonomy-working-group).

No draft text, reporting obligation, data requirement or issuance date is stated. It is the only standards instrument of any kind on this ledger, in a country whose transfer-pricing guidance has not been revised since 2018 and whose accessibility work exists as a toolbar on one ministry's own website.

summary: A [syndicate-backed freedom of information bill secured 60 signatures](2026-08-10-journalists-syndicate-submits-foi-bill-to-parliament); the regulator has a [consultation framework](2021-06-01-ntra-egypt-regulatory-framework-public-consultations).
developments:
2026-08-10 - a [syndicate-backed freedom of information bill was submitted after securing 60 lawmakers' signatures, proposing an authority for the protection of freedom of information](2026-08-10-journalists-syndicate-submits-foi-bill-to-parliament) - the clearest instance on this ledger of a non-governmental body carrying a legislative proposal into parliament.

The formal channel exists on paper: [the telecom regulator's bilingual framework for public consultations](2021-06-01-ntra-egypt-regulatory-framework-public-consultations). No consultation held under it, and no response document, is recorded.

An independent [analysis of 28,311 job postings](2026-04-07-eces-wp246-redefinition-of-work-in-egypt-ai-skill-demands) is research rather than policy input, and nothing records it being taken up.

progress: Mixed, a large complaints channel against low scores on user rights
summary: The complaints system received [195,000 items in one month](2025-10-08-unified-government-complaints-system-september-2025-report), while an assessment scores [5 of 40 on violations of user rights](2025-11-12-freedom-on-the-net-2025-egypt).
developments:
2025-10-08 - the unified government complaints system received [195,000 complaints, appeals, requests and enquiries in September 2025, of which 153,000 were routed to competent bodies](2025-10-08-unified-government-complaints-system-september-2025-report). It is a grievance channel operating on that volume, and nothing states what came back.

Against that, an international assessment scores the country [14 of 25 on obstacles to access, 9 of 35 on limits on content and 5 of 40 on violations of user rights](2025-11-12-freedom-on-the-net-2025-egypt), on a coverage period that ends before this window.

The participation measure sits between them: [an electronic participation index of 0.5890, ranked 74 of 193](2024-01-01-un-egovkb-country-information-egypt).

summary: [EGP 13bn of public investment was allocated to the sector in the 2025/26 plan](2026-08-07-egy-2025-ict-sector-dev-plan), and up to [US$860m a year is intended for data centres and state artificial intelligence](2026-08-21-egypttelegraph-860m-data-centre-budget).
developments:
No domestic appropriation was held at the window's opening. The [2025/26 plan presented to the House allocates EGP 13bn of public investment to the communications and information technology sector, against plan targets of US$8.5bn in annual digital exports of which US$6bn from outsourcing](2026-08-07-egy-2025-ict-sector-dev-plan), [reported separately](2026-08-07-egypt-ict-sector-development-plan-2025-2026). It is a plan allocation, not an outturn, and no execution figure against it is held.

2026-08-21 - a ministry document relayed at second hand states an [intended allocation of up to US$860 million a year from the general budget, from FY2026/27 to the end of 2030, for data centres, computing infrastructure, data security and privacy, and artificial-intelligence use inside state-owned companies, on a stated target of 0.10 to 0.15 per cent of national output](2026-08-21-egypttelegraph-860m-data-centre-budget). It is an intention with no appropriation line.

summary: The central bank [signed a memorandum on a pan-African gold bank](2025-12-30-cbe-afreximbank-mou-pan-african-gold-bank), and an [outsourcing delivery centre memorandum was signed](2026-07-06-ey-mena-egypt-ito-delivery-centre-itida-techafricanews).
developments:
2025-12-30 - a memorandum with a continental lender put a [pan-African gold bank at feasibility-study stage, to assess technical, commercial and regulatory requirements for siting it in a designated free zone with an internationally accredited refinery, secure vaulting and associated financial and trading services](2025-12-30-cbe-afreximbank-mou-pan-african-gold-bank).

2026-07-06 - a memorandum with the information technology agency framed [a regional outsourcing delivery centre serving Middle East and North Africa clients in consulting, risk management, cybersecurity, digital engineering, data analytics, artificial intelligence and business platforms, stated as creating more than 1,000 jobs over three years](2026-07-06-ey-mena-egypt-ito-delivery-centre-itida-techafricanews), with no investment sum, site or opening date.

The central bank also [offered its continental payment-system accession experience, currency-circulation system and institute training to Eswatini](2026-07-21-egypt-eswatini-central-banks-digital-payments), with [no instrument signed](2026-07-21-egypt-eswatini-deepen-banking-cooperation), and [talks with the United Kingdom covered digital skills, artificial intelligence, cloud, data centres and financial technology with no agreement stated](2026-01-15-egypt-uk-ict-cooperation-itweb). A [payments company signed an integration connecting its acceptance terminals with a point-of-sale software provider's system, targeting hospitality, retail chains and hypermarkets, with no sums, merchant counts or transaction volumes disclosed](2026-07-21-fawry-crystal-mind-pos-digital-payments).

summary: A [lender raised US$37.1m of equity and local-currency debt](2026-06-08-blnk-37m-raise-consumer-lending-techcabal), and the [startup charter began issuing label certificates](2026-08-10-umami-egypt-ai-learning-operating-system).
developments:
2026-06 - a consumer lender raised [US$12.5m of Series A equity led by a domestic venture fund with three development and regional investors, plus US$24.6m in local-currency debt from three Egyptian banks, against a point-of-sale lending network of more than 3,000 merchants, the company stating that around three quarters of its clients had never borrowed in the formal market](2026-06-08-blnk-37m-raise-consumer-lending-techcabal).

The charter was [a framework in preparation in December 2025, with a stated unified financing initiative of EGP 50bn to support 5,000 startups against targets of US$5bn of investment over five years and 500,000 jobs, and no launch, appropriation or governing instrument on file](2025-12-19-egypt-startup-ecosystem-2025-charter-techcabal). Certification is now [issuing, one company named among the first awarded the label, assessed on innovation, technological reliance, scalability and investment readiness](2026-08-10-umami-egypt-ai-learning-operating-system); no cumulative count, appropriation or disbursement figure accompanies it.

The largest listed payments company reports [2025 revenue of EGP 8.65bn and a market capitalisation of EGP 67.72bn on about six million transactions a day](2026-04-20-fawry-1bn-fintech-profile-techcabal).

summary: A development bank [lent up to EGP 250m to a payments company's small-business arm](2026-04-27-ebrd-fawry-2026-youth-msme-egypt) under a youth credit line in April 2026.
developments:
2026-04-27 - a development bank [lent up to EGP 250m, about EUR 4.4m, to a payments company's small-business finance arm under a youth credit line, with European cash incentives of up to 10 per cent of the loan amount](2026-04-27-ebrd-eu-fawry-youth-msme-egypt).

The standing instruments are larger and older: [a US$200m partial guarantee for sustainable transport and digital infrastructure](2023-09-22-aiib-egy-2023-egypt-transport-digital-infrastructure-guarantee), whose monitoring report [records formal consent in October 2025 to use bond proceeds for revised eligible subprojects](2025-11-01-aiib-egypt-sustainable-transport-digital-infrastructure-guarantee-pimr), and [a health insurance loan of 2020](2020-06-16-world-bank-egy-2020-uhis-loan).

progress: Mixed, fifth-generation service is in place across four operators and towers are expanding while measured combined download speeds fell below the pre-launch baseline
summary: [Fifth-generation service has run since June 2025 on refarmed 2.6 GHz](2026-08-03-ookla-5g-north-africa-one-year-on), while [combined median download speed fell to 34.77 Mbps](2026-08-03-ookla-5g-north-africa-one-year-on).
developments:
Service has been [in place since June 2025, initially focused on Cairo and Alexandria, on shared refarmed blocks of 20 to 30 MHz](2025-11-21 Egypt ICT and Digital Economy (US Country Commercial Guide)); no coverage obligation, subscriber count or population-coverage figure is held, and the country is the only one of four North African launch markets with no published coverage or quality obligation.

Crowdsourced measurement puts [fifth-generation median download at about 89 Mbps at month six against 110.5 Mbps on launch day, and the combined median at 34.77 Mbps against a pre-launch baseline of 37.68 Mbps, with fourth-generation down 17%](2026-08-03-ookla-5g-north-africa-one-year-on) - cited as a measurement, not absorbed.

[About 3,000 new towers are planned in 2026 and more than 9,000 over three years, against a target of 40,000 by 2028](2026-06-02-egypt-6bn-telecom-investment-since-2019-techafricanews). 2026-08-19 - a [first upper 6 GHz mobile trial ran at a reported 1.7 Gbps per user, with no allocation, award or commercial date](2026-08-19-telecom-egypt-6ghz-spectrum-trial).

summary: Fixed broadband reached [12.60 million subscriptions in November 2025, growing 8.98% year on year](2025-12-01-2africa-boosts-egypt-digital-exports-internet-costs-ahram).
developments:
The base held [11.51 million fixed broadband subscriptions for 2024](2025-12-01-2africa-boosts-egypt-digital-exports-internet-costs-ahram). By November 2025 there were [12.60 million, up from 12.50 million in October, growing 8.98% annually, with mobile carrying 75.44% of internet access against 72.97% a year earlier](2025-12-01-2africa-boosts-egypt-digital-exports-internet-costs-ahram).

The same monthly bulletin records [rising consumer complaints over data caps, upgrade fees and post-cap speed reduction](2025-12-01-2africa-boosts-egypt-digital-exports-internet-costs-ahram). So subscriptions grow while the terms attached to them draw complaint, and no later monthly figure than November 2025 is held.

progress: Mixed, the cheapest entry package fell while the rest of the ladder rose
summary: A [new mobile package at EGP 5 replaces one at about EGP 13](2026-05-06-ntra-egypt-digital-inclusion-packages-price-adjustment) while other packages rise 9 to 15%.
developments:
2026-05-06 - [a new mobile package at EGP 5 replaces a lowest package of about EGP 13, and a fixed package at EGP 150 replaces one at EGP 210, while other packages rise 9 to 15 per cent including taxes](2026-05-06-ntra-egypt-digital-inclusion-packages-price-adjustment).

The cheapest entry point falls and the rest of the ladder goes up, which is a distributional change rather than a price cut, and the regulator frames it as digital inclusion.

No data-basket price, no price index and no affordability measure against income appears anywhere on this ledger, so what the adjustment means for a typical subscriber cannot be stated. The regulator's [consultation framework](2021-06-01-ntra-egypt-regulatory-framework-public-consultations) is the process behind decisions of this kind.

summary: The incumbent [launched in-home fibre-to-the-room commercially with a vendor](2026-05-24-telecom-egypt-huawei-fttr-launch-ahram), stated as a first for the country.
developments:
The service did not exist at the window's opening. 2026-05-24 - the incumbent's consumer brand [launched in-home fibre-to-the-room commercially with a vendor, presented as a first for the country](2026-05-24-telecom-egypt-huawei-fttr-launch-ahram).

No coverage, subscriber, tariff or contract-value figure is stated. It is the only fixed-network product launch on this ledger, against a rural fibre programme that has reached about five million lines and a fixed base of about 12.6 million subscriptions - so what share of the network it touches is not established.

summary: [About fifteen active international submarine systems land in the country, the largest concentration in Africa](2025-12-01-2africa-boosts-egypt-digital-exports-internet-costs-ahram), and a [200 km, 5 Pbps link to Taba](2026-09-04-developingtelecoms-egypt-taba-red2med-cable) is under agreement.
developments:
The base held [thirteen systems landing on the eastern coast with a stated plan to expand to eighteen](2024-11-18 Telecom Egypt Regional Data Hub 2 awarded Tier III design certification), and now [about fifteen active systems, the largest concentration in Africa](2025-12-01-2africa-boosts-egypt-digital-exports-internet-costs-ahram). Both figures are operator or ministry-reported and no independent register is held.

The largest system carries [Mediterranean capacity in service since January 2025 on the Port Said to Genoa and Marseille route, with the country a transit hub rather than a terminal landing, the whole stated at about 45,000 km across thirty-three or more countries and designed for up to 180 Tbps on main routes](2025-01-23-telecom-egypt-cisco-2africa-mediterranean-ahram). [No later source updates the vendor partnership behind that activation](2025-01-23-telecom-egypt-cisco-2africa-mediterranean-ahram).

[An agreement was signed on 3 September 2026 to construct a multiple-petabit Sharm El Sheikh to Taba subsea cable, framed by the incumbent as extending the country's eastern digital corridor](2026-09-03-telecom-egypt-sharm-el-sheikh-taba-subsea-cable). It is a domestic route rather than an international landing, and no cost or in-service date is held.

summary: [15% of popular web content is served from inside the country, the majority from European servers](2026-06-09 Beyond the Homepage Measuring What It Really Takes to Keep Web Traffic Local).
developments:
A byte-weighted measurement puts [15% of popular web content served locally, the majority from European servers, against 13% for Algeria, 66% for South Africa and 83% for the United States](2026-06-09 Beyond the Homepage Measuring What It Really Takes to Keep Web Traffic Local). No prior reading is held.

The finding sits against the cable-hub and data-centre framing: the country carries other people's transit and hosts little of its own users' content. The one edge presence on file is a [content-delivery edge location in Cairo in operation since May 2024, with a vendor-stated latency reduction of up to about 30%, and no capacity expansion or additional presence recorded](2024-05-22 AWS adds a CloudFront edge location in Cairo) - an edge cache, not a cloud region.

summary: [Satellite talks moved to a licensed local operator with no licence, entity or service date](2026-04-30-egypt-online-telecom-starlink-talks-egypttelegraph), a possible 2025 launch having passed.
developments:
[Advanced ministry negotiations were reported in June 2025 with a possible launch during that year](2025-06-18-egypt-starlink-mcit-negotiations-egypttelegraph). That expectation passed without delivery. [Talks moved to a licensed local operator, with no licence, no local entity, no service date, and the operator's own map listing the country as service date unknown in May 2026](2026-04-30-egypt-online-telecom-starlink-talks-egypttelegraph); nothing is held on a June 2026 meeting or after.

The standing instrument is a [framework in force since 9 July 2024 for any foreign satellite operator serving earth-station terminals in the country, granting categorical licences to operators supplying space capacity to licensed providers](2024-07-09-egypt-ntra-foreign-satellite-framework-dpa), [adopted in October 2023 with a grace period](2023-10-08-egypt-ntra-satellite-operator-regulatory-framework). No foreign low-earth-orbit operator has been licensed under it, and the telecommunications law criminalises unlicensed wireless equipment with a minimum of one year's imprisonment.

summary: [Ten data-centre licences were issued over two years](2026-06-16-hassan-allam-400m-data-centre-license-wearetech), and the government's AI data-centre build is [contested between a Chinese vendor's bid and a United States consortium](2026-09-04-egypt-sovereignty-huawei-us-ai-tender-thecube) with no award on file.
developments:
The base holds no licence count or list at the window's opening. [Ten licences were issued over the preceding two years, with the regulator stated to be continuing to expand issuance](2026-06-16-hassan-allam-400m-data-centre-license-wearetech), the tenth [going to a contractor developing with a technology partner on a stated initial US$400m first-phase investment, with no site, capacity or opening date stated](2026-06-16-hassan-allam-400m-data-centre-license-wearetech). No licence register, licensee list or licence conditions are held.

One campus is [reported at 25 MW operating with plans to expand to 45 MW, among Africa's largest operational facilities, against continental capacity of over 500 MW operational and 890 MW in the pipeline](2026-07-28-africa-data-centre-capacity-500mw-890mw-pipeline), and an [expansion by a regional operator is named in that pipeline with no site, capacity, investment figure or date given](2026-07-28-africa-data-centre-capacity-500mw-890mw-pipeline).

progress: Mixed, the incumbent's second regional hub passed its stated completion date unconfirmed while the sale of a majority stake in its data-centre unit was cancelled and the unit brought back in-house
summary: The [second regional hub is now put one to two months from operating](2026-08-28-fintechgate-telecom-egypt-rdh2-data-centre) after its end-2025 date passed unconfirmed, and a [majority-stake sale was cancelled](2026-07-17-telecom-egypt-cancels-helios-data-center-stake-sale).
developments:
The second hub was [design-certified to Tier III with an estimated IT load of 4.6 MW against the first hub's 2.5 MW and completion expected end-2025](2024-11-18 Telecom Egypt Regional Data Hub 2 awarded Tier III design certification). No held source states it entered service, and the stated date has passed; the first hub is stated as reaching full utilisation within a year of opening.

2026-07-17 - the board [withdrew from an agreement announced in September 2025 to sell 75 to 80% of the regional data-centre hub, citing unmet conditions, and the hub is instead to be carved out as a wholly-owned subsidiary with its own technical and commercial team](2026-07-17-telecom-egypt-cancels-helios-data-center-stake-sale). Consideration and the specific unmet conditions are not disclosed, and the stated reason is transactional rather than sovereigntist.

2026-08-28 - the chief executive told the half-year results call that [phase two is expected to begin operating within one to two months, on economics improved against phase one, with further projects screened on internal rate of return, payback period and business model](2026-08-28-fintechgate-telecom-egypt-rdh2-data-centre); the carve-out into a wholly owned subsidiary continues and the chief financial officer said retaining the business is worth more than the cancelled sale. No entry into service is stated, and this is a second schedule against a first that passed.

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: The [government cloud centre is described as an active alternative to the new capital data centre](2024-04-28-egypt-government-data-cloud-computing-center-p1-inauguration); no replication is stated.
developments:
The [government data and cloud computing centre was inaugurated in April 2024 and described as an active alternative to the new capital data centre and as a unified national platform](2024-04-28-egypt-government-data-cloud-computing-center-p1-inauguration). Two sites described as alternatives to each other is the closest thing to off-site capacity the base holds.

What is not stated anywhere is what is replicated between them, on what schedule, to what recovery objective, or whether a restore has been tested.

2026-03-26 - the electricity and communications ministers [agreed a joint task force to draw up a national data-centre strategy covering investment incentives, licensing, land and energy](2026-03-26-electricity-ict-ministers-data-centre-industry-development).

summary: A [hyperscale data centre approaching US$1bn is proposed for Sinai on seawater cooling and green hydrogen power](2026-03-17-egypt-sinai-hyperscale-data-centre-renergy-ahram).
developments:
Neither the project nor its power arrangement existed at the window's opening. 2026-03-17 - a proposal put to the investment minister targets [investment approaching US$1bn, starting at 10,000 square metres with an expansion vision to 500,000, seawater cooling, and power wholly from the consortium's green hydrogen and solar project, the minister requiring a full feasibility, financing structure and shareholder file, and coordination with three ministries and security bodies](2026-03-17-egypt-sinai-hyperscale-data-centre-renergy-ahram). It is talks, not a project.

The power source is [about 127 square kilometres with 4 km of Red Sea frontage, EUR 5m of technical studies completed over two years, two phases targeting 160,000 then 400,000 tonnes a year of liquid green hydrogen wholly for export to Europe](2026-03-17-egypt-sinai-hyperscale-data-centre-renergy-ahram) - the only data-centre power arrangement of any kind in the base, and it is a proposal whose output is contracted elsewhere.

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: The electricity holding company's [annual report carries capacity, peak load and the state load-reduction plan](2024-06-30-eehc-egypt-annual-report-2023-2024).
developments:
The [holding company's own annual report for the year to 30 June 2024 carries installed capacity, peak load and generation figures and the state load-reduction plan that shaped the year](2024-06-30-eehc-egypt-annual-report-2023-2024). It is the only systematic account of grid performance the base holds, and it is two years old.

A load-reduction plan is the reliability position stated in the government's own terms. No interruption duration or frequency index is published, and no figure since 2024 appears anywhere - which matters because [the data-centre strategy the ministers agreed in March 2026 covers energy](2026-03-26-electricity-ict-ministers-data-centre-industry-development).

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: The [rural development programme completed works in 620 villages](2026-01-06-egypt-haya-karima-phase-one-implementation-review); no electrification rate is held.
developments:
The dated review of the rural development programme's first phase records [EGP 306bn allocated, 93% of total first-phase investments, with development works completed in 620 villages](2026-01-06-egypt-haya-karima-phase-one-implementation-review), against an earlier account of [EGP 350bn allocated and EGP 200bn disbursed across 23,000 projects](2023-01-01-mped-egypt-decent-life-first-phase-implementation-status).

Neither states an electrification rate, a connection count or a rural-urban access split, so what the programme has done to electricity access cannot be stated. Its digital component is the technology equipment [supplied to the government service complexes in those villages](2025-05-30-mcit-hayah-karima-government-service-complexes-technology-agreement).

summary: An [institutional memory system is being taken to individual state bodies](2026-08-17-ahramgate-nppa-institutional-memory-system), and a [unified manufacturers platform launched](2026-08-19-sis-egypt-unified-manufacturers-platform).
developments:
Neither existed at the window's opening. A cabinet information centre system for institutional memory is [being taken to individual state bodies: the nuclear power plants authority received a delegation on it as part of its digital transformation](2026-08-17-ahramgate-nppa-institutional-memory-system), and the [social solidarity ministry held an expanded meeting on its objectives and components ahead of applying it](2026-08-19-dostor-social-solidarity-institutional-memory). No adoption count, technical description or completion date is published.

2026-08-19 - an industry ministry [platform launched covering the industrial investment cycle, carrying a complaints-management system with defined response deadlines and real-time indicators on resolution rates and recurring issues, a database and marketplace for locally produced production inputs, and a separate marketplace for finished industrial products](2026-08-19-sis-egypt-unified-manufacturers-platform); no registration count or service-level standard is published.

summary: A [career-launch initiative covers cybersecurity, development operations and telecom networks](2025-09-11-mcit-nti-egypt-cit-career-launch-initiative), on a [four-pillar civil-service programme](2025-01-01-mcit-states-administrative-apparatus-employees-programs).
developments:
The standing programme for civil-service digital capability runs on [four pillars: digital culture, digital skills, the skills of information-centre employees and leadership](2025-01-01-mcit-states-administrative-apparatus-employees-programs).

2025-09-11 - a [career-launch initiative covers cybersecurity, development operations and telecom networks - the three skill areas bearing most directly on maintaining and operating government systems](2025-09-11-mcit-nti-egypt-cit-career-launch-initiative), and a [summer programme was designed for 10,000 students across eight tracks](2025-09-15-itida-nti-egypt-summer-training-program-first-phase).

2026-02-09 - the [sixth batch of an artificial-intelligence ambassadors programme graduated 2,641 trainees](2026-02-09-nti-ese-sixth-batch-ai-ambassadors-program). No in-house-versus-contractor split for government systems is published.

summary: The [second-edition cybersecurity strategy is being implemented with a third in preparation](2026-06-10-egypt-ai-national-security-strategy-karnak-ahram), and the country holds a [full score on the global index](2025-02-18 Egypt scores 100% on the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index (2024)).
developments:
The base carries no dated statement of which strategy edition was in force at the window's opening. The [second edition is being implemented through projects to protect digital infrastructure and build cyber defences, a third is being prepared, and the national emergency readiness centre is being developed to use artificial intelligence against cyber threats](2026-06-10-egypt-ai-national-security-strategy-karnak-ahram). No edition dates, text or publication is held: the whole position rests on one ministerial statement to a Senate committee.

The readiness centre [operates under the telecommunications regulator and is a delivery partner in the national cyber-skills academy](2026-07-06-nti-cybersecurity-academy-6000-trainees-ahram), with no incident statistics, mandate document, budget or reporting obligation held.

The [global index standing of 100% and a first-tier place among twelve states](2025-02-18 Egypt scores 100% on the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index (2024)) was restated in June 2026, but both readings refer to the same 2024 edition, so it is a static reading rather than movement.

summary: The government digital switch [connects 105 bodies and links 100 national databases](2026-07-19-ahram-pm-presidential-directives-digital-transformation), and a digital treasury of reusable documents began.
developments:
The base carries no connection count, architecture statement or lawful basis for the exchange at the window's opening. The switch now has [105 government bodies connected and 100 national databases linked for secure inter-agency exchange, named alongside unified digital identity, the services platform, the digital treasury, digital trust services and the digital post box as the enablers of the transformation](2026-07-19-ahram-pm-presidential-directives-digital-transformation). It is ministry-reported through a cabinet readout: no published register of connected bodies, no lawful basis, no audit arrangement and no role for a data-protection regulator is held.

The [digital treasury's operating model is set and applied to a number of services, its first output the registration certificate as a verified reusable document consumed by the shop-licensing service, implementing the once-only principle](2026-07-27-almal-tarakhis-almahal-alamma-misr-digital-platform-licensing); no list of documents, count of reuses or governing instrument is held.

2026-08-20 - a [protocol will integrate the commercial registry and stock exchange databases, giving the exchange direct access to registry data for listed companies, with a joint executive committee overseeing implementation and data confidentiality](2026-08-20-businessmen-eg-egx-itda-data-integration).

summary: Two services launched in the same week gate access on the [national digital identity](2026-09-01-egypte-parquet-service-electronique-affaires-familiales) — family-case enquiry and [foster-family services](2026-08-29-egypte-solidarite-services-numeriques-familles-adoptives).
developments:
The public prosecution opened an electronic enquiry service for family-case data and judgments on 1 September 2026, with entry restricted to users verified through the national digital identity so the data reaches only the party concerned ([service](2026-09-01-egypte-parquet-service-electronique-affaires-familiales)).

The social solidarity ministry launched the first phase of a digital services system for foster families and care institutions two days earlier, wired to other state bodies through the government digital exchange and to the national digital identity for sign-in ([launch](2026-08-29-egypte-solidarite-services-numeriques-familles-adoptives)).

Both are single services rather than a general integration, and neither publishes a transaction figure. What they establish is that the identity is now a precondition of reaching one's own record in two ministries.

summary: The health insurance information system's [beneficiary, provider and claims modules are not yet in service](2026-01-20-worldbank-isr-supporting-egypt-uhis-p172426-seq11).
developments:
The health data layer under universal health insurance carries [4.5 million electronic health records, a unified electronic medical record and an electronic prescription](2024-08-19-eha-pillars-of-digital-transformation-telemedicine-uhis), and the health cooperation strategy [records interoperability with the national identification systems](2025-01-01-who-egypt-country-cooperation-strategy-2024-2028).

2026-01-20 - a supervision report states [the procurement module developed and in service, with the beneficiary, provider and claims modules not yet in service](2026-01-20-worldbank-isr-supporting-egypt-uhis-p172426-seq11) - the three an exchange would run over.

2025-12 - a memorandum [would automate the healthcare accreditation authority's core operations](2025-12-02-mcit-gahar-mou-digital-institutional-development).

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: A [unified pre-university education dataset complies with the statistics agency's requirements](2025-12-15-moete-unified-national-pre-university-education-data-ed1-ed50); no other exchange is held.
developments:
2025-12-15 - the [first unified national infrastructure for pre-university education data was launched, complying with the statistics agency's requirements](2025-12-15-moete-unified-national-pre-university-education-data-ed1-ed50). That compliance is the one education-system exchange the base holds, and it runs to the statistical system rather than between education systems.

2026-04-01 - the communications and higher education ministries [set out a digital transformation agenda including issuing digital graduation certificates through the national platform](2026-04-01-mcit-mohesr-ministers-education-technology-cooperation) - an exchange in prospect, with no certificate volume or start date.

summary: The regulator [referred all four mobile operators to prosecution over lines registered without their holders' knowledge](2026-08-10-egypt-sim-reverification-operators-prosecution) and expanded facial verification.
developments:
The base carries no position on mobile line registration at the window's opening. 2026-08-10 - the regulator [referred all four operators to the Public Prosecution over lines registered without customers' knowledge, ordered them to halt new activations on corporate registration systems, contact every existing corporate-line holder to re-register in person by a deadline with unclaimed lines cancelled, and accelerate biometric verification, warning that non-compliance would cost them sale and activation rights](2026-08-10-egypt-sim-reverification-operators-prosecution). It followed [reports of a nineteen-year-old sentenced in absentia to twenty-five years in a case turning on a line registered in his name](2026-08-13-egypt-expands-biometric-sim-registration-after-identity-misuse-case).

The regulator [logged over 3,000 line-fraud complaints and 100,000 call-centre inquiries in two days](2026-08-10-egypt-ntra-phone-line-fraud-complaints), and [public use of its line-checking service reached five million registrations in a week, roughly doubling its user base](2026-08-17-egypt-sim-verification-5-million-users). Members [asked what framework governs collection, storage and access to the facial-recognition data taken at registration](2026-08-17-egypt-mp-facial-recognition-concerns), and [researchers argue irreversible biometrics carry their own risk while the protection framework is still being built](2026-08-12-egypt-privacy-chaos-sim-biometric-critique).

summary: Electronic registration of births and deaths is [stated as taken nationwide](2026-08-02-egypt-development-plan-digital-transformation-population-file), and civil-registry kiosks stand at sixteen locations.
developments:
The base carries no statement on electronic civil registration coverage at the window's opening. The health ministry and associated bodies are [stated to have taken electronic registration of births and deaths nationwide, credited with faster and more accurate demographic monitoring](2026-08-02-egypt-development-plan-digital-transformation-population-file). Nationwide is the plan's own word: no coverage rate, completeness figure or target date is reported, the plan document is not held, and the claim is uncorroborated.

The [sixteen mall-based kiosks across six governorates and the airport, issuing birth, death, marriage and divorce certificates and identity application forms on fingerprint or facial verification and paid in cash, are unchanged, with no expansion, transaction count or withdrawal recorded](2024-09-24 Egypt deploys automated civil-registry kiosks (birth certificates and national ID)).

summary: The interior ministry [created a unified national biometric verification platform](2026-02-14-moi-mansat-al-tahaqquq-al-biyumitri-wal-musadaqa), it states for the first time.
developments:
2026-02-14 - the interior ministry [states it has created, for the first time in the country, a unified national platform for biometric verification and instant authentication using face-recognition algorithms](2026-02-14-moi-mansat-al-tahaqquq-al-biyumitri-wal-musadaqa). No lawful basis, retention rule, accuracy figure or oversight arrangement is stated with it.

2026-08-23 - the central bank board [approved regulations governing the digital financial identity platform for identifying bank customers and verifying identities electronically](2026-08-23-cbe-digital-financial-identity-platform-ekyc-regulations).

2025-09-10 - a [citizens' data update form was launched in one governorate as the initial phase of a nationwide expansion](2025-09-10-mcit-citizen-data-update-form-port-said) - the maintenance side of the register.

summary: The [national digital identity app reached a second release adding biometric verification and liveness detection](2026-07-19-ahram-pm-presidential-directives-digital-transformation), integrated with e-signature and e-seal.
developments:
A [digital identity card enabling remote verification was under development](2025-12-18 Egypt targets full government automation and digital ID verification by 2026). The app is now [released and in its second version, integrated with electronic signature and seal services, with civil-registry-linked verification stated as approaching](2026-05-20-egypt-digital-id-ekyc-esignature-approaching-youm7). No registration count, first-release date or governing decree is held.

[Signature and seal services are live using the security token and integrated with digital identity, with remote signature stated as expanding across government services and the digital post box being finalised](2026-07-19-ahram-pm-presidential-directives-digital-transformation).

2026-02 - an [interior ministry Android pilot has users scan the identity card and complete facial recognition to authenticate for selected government services, with scaling to be decided on the pilot's outcome](2026-03-10-egypt-moieg-pass-selfie-biometrics-pilot-biometricupdate); it was [described at launch as the country's first unified biometric authentication platform](2026-02-14 Egypt Interior Ministry launches MOIEG-PASS biometric verification app), which is hard to reconcile with the central bank's own system three months earlier.

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: An [electronic birth and death registration system was recorded as under way from 2017](2019-10-14-uneca-electronic-birth-and-death-registration-system-in-egypt); no identifier at birth is stated.
developments:
An [electronic birth and death registration system was recorded as under way from 2017](2019-10-14-uneca-electronic-birth-and-death-registration-system-in-egypt), and the country's own submission puts [birth registration completeness at 96.6%](2024-01-01-egypt-unsd-vital-statistics-questionnaire-2024).

Registration is close to complete and nothing states that an identifier is issued at the birth event, or that the civil status system and the identity system exchange at that point. The country's [own presentation contrasting 2017 with 2026](2026-07-17-egypt-crvs-journey-2017-2026) is the fullest account held and it does not close that question.

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: The health cooperation strategy [records interoperability with the national identification systems](2025-01-01-who-egypt-country-cooperation-strategy-2024-2028); no birth-registration link is stated.
developments:
The one interoperability with the identification systems the base holds is on the health side: [the health cooperation strategy records it](2025-01-01-who-egypt-country-cooperation-strategy-2024-2028).

On the civil registration side, [the electronic birth and death registration system recorded as under way from 2017](2019-10-14-uneca-electronic-birth-and-death-registration-system-in-egypt) and the [country's own 2017-to-2026 presentation](2026-07-17-egypt-crvs-journey-2017-2026) describe the registration system without stating a link to the identity system.

The new biometric platform is a verification service rather than a registration one: [unified national biometric verification and instant authentication](2026-02-14-moi-mansat-al-tahaqquq-al-biyumitri-wal-musadaqa).

summary: The central bank [approved rules for a digital financial identity](2026-08-23-ahram-egypt-central-bank-digital-financial-identity-rules), and the Prosecution [opened criminal-record self-enquiry through digital identity](2026-07-27-ahram-public-prosecution-electronic-criminal-record-enquiry-egypt).
developments:
2026-08-23 - the central bank's board [approved rules for the digital financial identity system: customers may open accounts and take banking products through digital channels without visiting a branch, with electronic acceptance of terms and electronic authentication in place of a handwritten signature, the rules setting out governance, participants' roles, technical and operational requirements and data-protection and cybersecurity controls](2026-08-23-ahram-egypt-central-bank-digital-financial-identity-rules), the system having been [launched in November 2025](2025-11-13 Egypt CBE launches Haweya national digital financial ID (eKYC)). No enrolment or verification volume is held.

On the non-bank side, [lending, investment and insurance companies may create digital identities, run biometric and non-biometric checks against national-identity and mobile-registry databases and execute binding electronic contracts, the licensee reporting over 25m verifications a year](2025-08-11-digified-ekyc-esignature-fra-license-biometricupdate).

2026-07-27 - a citizen may now [query criminal judgments registered against their own national number through the digital identity system, the Prosecution stating the result is not a substitute for official certificates](2026-07-27-ahram-public-prosecution-electronic-criminal-record-enquiry-egypt).

summary: The central bank gave [initial approval to a first wholly digital bank](2025-08-18-cbe-first-digital-bank-onebank-itweb) and [preliminary approval to a second](2026-08-21-tan-cib-yomo-digital-bank-egypt); neither is operating.
developments:
The first had [preliminary clearance from May 2024 with due diligence on infrastructure, banking systems and cybersecurity under way](2025-08-18-cbe-first-digital-bank-onebank-itweb); initial approval was granted with products stated as preparing for 2026 and no launch on record, so nothing held establishes an operating digital bank in the country.

2026-08-21 - a commercial bank received [preliminary approval to establish a digitally native bank under the 2023 digital-banks framework, now entering technology validation, cybersecurity testing and operational-resilience readiness under a newly appointed chief executive, launch remaining subject to final approval, with no launch date or capitalisation stated](2026-08-21-tan-cib-yomo-digital-bank-egypt).

Two approvals and no operating institution is the position after two years of the framework.

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: A [completion report closes a US$900m safety-net loan](2024-06-05-worldbank-icr-strengthening-social-safety-net-project-egypt); no current payment channel figure is held.
developments:
The arrangements are described in [a country note on government-to-person payments, which sets out the flagship cash transfer programme launched in 2015](2021-06-23-worldbank-g2p-payment-arrangements-in-egypt-and-covid-19).

2024-06-05 - a completion report [closes a US$900m-equivalent loan strengthening the safety net](2024-06-05-worldbank-icr-strengthening-social-safety-net-project-egypt).

Neither states a current beneficiary count, a payment channel split or a digital-payment share, so what proportion of transfers now reach people electronically is not on the base - against a [financial inclusion rate of 77.6% at the end of 2025](2026-02-17-cbe-second-financial-inclusion-strategy-2026-2030).

progress: Mixed, a second facilitation package added a services centre and a real-estate app while named defects in the tax system remain on the record and the 2018 transfer-pricing guide is unrevised
summary: A [second facilitation package added a premium centre and a real-estate transactions app](2026-08-19-sis-egypt-tax-services-centre-realestate-app), against [named defects still on the record](2026-07-29-alborsa-tax-digitisation-comprehensive-reform-assessment-egypt).
developments:
The tax system has run since January 2021 across returns, electronic invoices and receipts, registration, payments, automated audit, refunds, exemptions, appeals and enforced collection. 2026-08-19 - a [second facilitation package added a premium services centre and a real-estate transactions app on which citizens register transaction details, upload documents, pay taxes and obtain electronic clearance certificates online, with telephone guidance for less confident users](2026-08-19-sis-egypt-tax-services-centre-realestate-app); no uptake figure is published.

The defects are named by practitioners: [historic credit balances never migrated so companies holding credits are shown as debtors; audit offices demanding paper copies of documents already on the authority's databases; files moved to appeal committees on timer expiry; some payments unevidenceable, creating phantom debts; and government bodies not always issuing electronic invoices while the private sector is compelled to](2026-07-29-alborsa-tax-digitisation-comprehensive-reform-assessment-egypt).

The [2018 transfer-pricing guide is unrevised, with appeal committees relying on the statutory requirement for a minister-approved guide and some penalties cancelled as a result](2026-07-29-alborsa-tax-digitisation-comprehensive-reform-assessment-egypt), and a [proposed cut of the VAT credit-refund period awaits its legislative steps](2026-07-29-alborsa-tax-digitisation-comprehensive-reform-assessment-egypt).

summary: A [digital factoring portal lets companies verify prior funding of an invoice electronically](2026-08-06-egypt-fra-digitizing-factoring-platform), enforcing a ban on double-funding a receivable.
developments:
There was no electronic check on whether an invoice had already been funded. Factoring companies now [verify prior funding electronically through a direct link with the finance ministry and the tax authority, the platform vetting invoices before financing and freezing them to the financing company to enforce a board resolution's ban on double-funding a receivable, with a second phase to make the full cycle electronic undated](2026-08-06-egypt-fra-digitizing-factoring-platform); companies were [trained on it on 6 August 2026](2026-02-08 Egypt FRA launches digital factoring portal). [Factored paper value rose 77.8% in 2025 to EGP 132.2bn](2026-08-06-egypt-fra-digitizing-factoring-platform).

2026-08-13 - the [state digital financial infrastructure operator agreed the full acquisition of a non-bank lender to small and medium firms, extending its own infrastructure into direct lending](2026-08-13-egypt-efinance-tamweely-acquisition), with [no consideration disclosed](2026-08-13-efinance-tamweely-2026-efinance-acquires-tamweely-financial-services); the record states no separation between its role building and running government payment infrastructure and the lending book it is buying.

summary: The central bank [launched acceptance on merchants' own phones](2026-02-01 Egypt CBE launches SoftPOS contactless payment-acceptance service), and a [first carrier-billing licence covers government payments](2025-12-11 tpay secures NTRA licence for direct mobile payments for government services).
developments:
Phone-based acceptance was [a pilot capped at EGP 600 per transaction](2026-02-01 Egypt CBE launches SoftPOS contactless payment-acceptance service) and is now live: merchants may use a smartphone or tablet as an electronic point of sale, accepting contactless card payments with the customer entering a PIN on the device. No merchant count, transaction volume or cap for the live service is held.

2025-12-11 - a [first regulator licence for direct carrier billing was signed, letting citizens pay utility bills, traffic fines and civil-registry charges from mobile balance or the monthly bill](2025-12-11 tpay secures NTRA licence for direct mobile payments for government services). No transaction volume, participating operator list or live-service date is held after signature.

summary: The instant payment network reached [16m users and EGP 4.2tn transacted to June 2025](2026-03-04-instapay-16m-users-4-2tn-ahram), alongside [over 55.5m wallet accounts](2026-07-24-elwatan-instapay-mobile-wallets-54-million-financial-inclusion).
developments:
The network had [12.5m users and about 1.5bn transactions worth up to EGP 2.9tn in calendar 2024, domestic transfers only](2024-12-30-cbe-instapay-fee-exemption-2024-volumes). It now has [16m users and EGP 4.2tn transacted from July 2024 to June 2025, with inbound remittances credited instantly at all banks operating in the country](2026-03-04-instapay-16m-users-4-2tn-ahram). No figure fresher than end-June 2025 is held.

Wallets stand at [over 55.5m accounts transacting about EGP 1.8tn to June 2025, growth telco-led through the three operators' products](2026-07-24-elwatan-instapay-mobile-wallets-54-million-financial-inclusion); a Senate proposal of June 2026 puts the base at 45m against about 6m bank cards, an unreconciled framing of the same stock.

Cards and acceptance stand at [29.1m debit cards at about 40% of the market, 34.3m prepaid, about 7m credit, over 26,000 cash machines and about 275,000 terminals, with national scheme cards still stated at 43.5m from end-2024](2025-11-17-cbe-meeza-instapay-wallets-inclusion-pafix-ahram). About [16.7 million adults had no formal access to credit at June 2025](2026-06-08-blnk-37m-raise-consumer-lending-techcabal).

summary: The continental settlement system is [headquartered in Cairo with no Egyptian participation, volume or value figure published](2022-05-11 Pan-African Payment and Settlement System).
developments:
The system has [operated from Cairo since January 2022, connecting the real-time gross settlement systems of participating African central banks, with twenty-five large commercial banks connected in 2022](2022-05-11 Pan-African Payment and Settlement System), and no Egyptian participation, volume or value figure has been published in anything held. The [lender behind it continues to frame it as the route to continental trade](2026-05-30 Afreximbank Banks on Digital Payments to Unlock Africa's Trillion-Dollar Trade Potential).

The only movement on the record is diplomatic: the central bank offering its accession experience to another state in July 2026. Inbound remittances now credit instantly at all banks through the domestic instant rail, which is the cross-border function actually measurable here, and it runs outside the continental system.

summary: [Instant-transfer fees stand where they were set in April 2025, at 0.1% of value with a EGP 20 cap](2025-03-31-instapay-fees-introduced-april-2025-ahram).
developments:
Pricing has been [0.1% with a minimum of EGP 0.50 and a maximum of EGP 20 since 1 April 2025, plus EGP 0.50 for balance enquiry beyond ten free monthly requests](2025-03-31-instapay-fees-introduced-april-2025-ahram), and no central-bank decision altering the schedule is held.

The prior free-use position [rested on a board exemption effective 1 January 2025 for three renewable months rather than on an instrument, and lapsed rather than being repealed](2024-12-30-cbe-instapay-fee-exemption-2024-volumes) - so the country's flagship retail rail moved from free to priced without a published decision to price it.

summary: Registration completeness is high on the country's own figures, and a [citizens' data update form was piloted in one governorate](2025-09-10-mcit-citizen-data-update-form-port-said).
developments:
The register rests on [the 1994 civil status law and the civil status organisation at the interior ministry](1994-06-09-qanun-143-lisanat-1994-fi-shan-al-ahwal-al-madaniyya), with [completeness put at 96.6% for live births and 95.3% for deaths](2024-01-01-egypt-unsd-vital-statistics-questionnaire-2024).

2025-09-10 - the communications and supply ministries [launched a citizens' data update form in one governorate as the initial phase of a gradual nationwide expansion, described as an organising instrument for keeping citizen records current](2025-09-10-mcit-citizen-data-update-form-port-said). No completion, record count or further governorate is recorded.

The 2027 census is [in preparation under a high committee the prime minister chairs](2026-02-02-prime-minister-chairs-high-committee-2027-census).

summary: Registration completeness is put at [96.6% for live births and 95.3% for deaths](2024-01-01-egypt-unsd-vital-statistics-questionnaire-2024) on the country's own submission.
developments:
